profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, CA, traded on the NASDAQ under the ticker NVDA. Its most recently reported annual revenue was $215,938,000,000 for the fiscal year ending January 25, 2026, as disclosed in a 10-K filing. The company develops hardware and software for artificial intelligence, data science, and accelerated computing.

On the AI software side, NVIDIA offers the Nemotron family of multimodal foundation models, which the company describes as designed for agentic reasoning across tasks including advanced math, graduate-level science, and visual understanding. The site presents Nemotron models as openly available, with published model weights, training datasets, and training techniques distributed under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which permits commercial use and modification without attribution. Specific models mentioned include NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, described as optimized for faster specialized task completion, and NeMo Switchyard, described as a routing component for directing agent steps to appropriate models. Nemotron models cover capability areas including reasoning, multimodal vision, retrieval-augmented generation, speech recognition and synthesis, neural machine translation, and safety. NVIDIA also offers NVIDIA NIM, a set of inference microservices for deploying foundation models in enterprise environments, available through build.nvidia.com and requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for production deployment. Bryan Catanzaro is identified on the site as Vice President of Applied Deep Learning Research at NVIDIA.

The held facts note no litigation or MCP server registrations on record for NVIDIA at this time.
